notes.title: The maelstrom
notes.drew: Off the tip of Lofoten, Olaus draws a great whirlpool swallowing a ship. He letters it Charybdis, after the monster of Homer's strait, and calls it horrible.
notes.was: Moskstraumen, between Lofotodden and the island of Mosken: a system of tidal eddies and small whirlpools in currents of about 2 to 5 metres a second. There is no single giant whirlpool.

notes.title: The sea serpent
notes.drew: A red serpent coiled round a ship off Helgeland, taking a sailor from the deck; the chart's key gives it 200 feet. In his Historia Olaus puts it in the caves near Bergen, and has its rising foretell upheaval in the kingdom.
notes.was: No such animal. The place is the Historia's Bergen, far to the south of where the chart draws the beast.

source.title: Olaus Magnus' sea serpent, The Public Domain Review

notes.title: The Lofoten stockfish
notes.drew: Bundles of dried fish on the Lofoten shore, and a line saying that here is the busiest fish market. In the Historia the fish are dried in the wind, piled like stacks of wood and shipped to Bergen to trade.
notes.was: The Lofoten winter cod fishery, whose fish were dried as stockfish and sold through Bergen. Vågan, by Kabelvåg, was the islands' first town.

source.title: A Compendious History of the Goths, Swedes, & Vandals (1658), Book 21
source.licence: Public domain (the 1658 text; the transcription's licence unverified)

notes.checked: text (Book 21: dried, piled, shipped to Bergen); web (Lofoten fishery, Vågan)

notes.title: Hekla
notes.drew: Flames under a mountain lettered Mons Hekla. Olaus tells of Iceland's mountains with snow on their tops and fire of brimstone at their feet, and of a rock that boils like Etna and is taken for the place of Hell.
notes.was: Hekla, the volcano medieval Europe called the gateway to Hell. It erupted in 1510, within Olaus's lifetime.
notes.checked: web (Hekla, 1510, gateway to Hell); text (Book 2: snow and brimstone, boils like Etna)

notes.title: Vardøhus
notes.drew: A walled house lettered Vardahus on Norway's far north-east shore, which the chart stretches up toward the pole.
notes.was: Vardøhus Fortress, first built by Haakon V in 1306 on Norway's border with Russia.

notes.title: The Tornio market and the Birkarls
notes.drew: By Tornio, at the head of the Gulf of Bothnia, the chart marks a great market with bales of goods beside it. Further west it draws the houses and the chiefs of the Birkarls.
notes.was: Tornio was the base of the Birkarls, a small group of traders who held the Sámi trade and its taxes from 1328 until the crown took them over in 1553.
notes.checked: web (Birkarls, Tornio their base); scan (the market's label, read at low resolution: unverified)

notes.title: The glutton
notes.drew: A beast gorging on a carcass, then squeezing between two trees to empty its belly so that it can eat again. The Historia gives this Gulo a chapter of its own.
notes.was: The wolverine, mostly a scavenger. Its name of glutton comes partly from a false etymology, the Norwegian fjellfross heard as the German Vielfraß, much-eater.
notes.checked: web (the animal, the etymology); text (the Historia's chapter of the Gulos)

notes.title: The White Lake
notes.drew: Lacus Albus, the White Lake: a closed water in the far east of the sheet, full of fish and birds, with boats on it.
notes.was: The White Sea, about 90,000 km², an inlet of the Barents Sea and open to it through the Gorlo strait.

notes.title: Tile
notes.drew: An island lettered Tile between the Orkneys and the Faroes, which the chart says holds thirty thousand people.
notes.was: No island lies there. Thule was the land Pytheas reached about 330 BC and no one found again; it has been read as Shetland, the Faroes, Iceland or Norway.
notes.checked: web (Thule); scan (the population, read off the chart's lettering)

notes.title: Hvitsark
notes.drew: A round rock lettered Hvitsark, west of Iceland. The Historia sets it half way from Iceland's west coast to Greenland.
notes.was: No such island. The Denmark Strait, about 290 km across at its narrowest, has none.
notes.checked: web (no such island, sv.wiki; the strait's width); text (half way)
